questions.q: Where do Opportunities and Cases meet in the Salesforce data model?
options: At the Lead
At the Account
At the Campaign
They never connect
questions.explain: Both Opportunities and Cases belong to an Account, so at-risk-deal questions are Account-level questions.

questions.q: A custom report type is best described as which structure?
options: A tree with unlimited sibling children
A single object only
A random collection of objects
A chain of related objects, so two unrelated siblings generally cannot be combined
questions.explain: Because it is a chain, you generally cannot put Opportunities and Cases side by side under Accounts. Confirm current limits in your org.

questions.q: What does an Accounts report with cross filters give you for the at-risk question?
options: A list of accounts meeting both conditions, but not summed Opportunity amounts
The exact dollar value at risk
A forecast of next quarter
The agent who owns each case
questions.explain: Cross filters return clean Account rows without multiplying them, but they do not sum child Opportunity amounts.

questions.q: A $50K opportunity sits on an account with three open cases. A report joining them shows the opportunity three times. What is this called and what is the risk?
options: Normalization, which improves accuracy
A cross filter, which hides rows
Fan-out, which can inflate sums of the parent's amount
Bucketing, which groups values
questions.explain: Joining a parent to multiple children repeats the parent's fields per child row, so summing Amount overstates the total.

questions.q: When is it reasonable to move from native reports to CRM Analytics or Tableau?
options: Always, for any dashboard
When you need row-level blending across many objects, outside data, or volume that strains native reports
Only when the dashboard has one chart
Never, native reports can do everything
questions.explain: These tools suit complex cross-object modeling and larger data, but they involve licensing and setup. For simple needs native tools may suffice.
